name: Apple
model: written by hand (Claude) from the Urdu KB

aspects.overview: Apple is a popular fruit, red, green or yellow, rich in vitamins A, B and C, with about 11 percent sugar. It started in the cold areas of South Asia; improved varieties came to Pakistan in British times. Apple needs a fairly long cold season and 550 to 650 mm of rain a year, spread evenly. Hail and long cold spells during flowering and fruit setting badly cut the crop. Best soil: deep, fertile loam with good drainage. Land with a hard sub-layer, salinity (kallar) or waterlogging (sem) is not suitable; poor drainage causes root diseases.
aspects.varieties:
Low-chill plains and milder areas such as Pothohar: Anna, Dorsett Golden and Gold Summer (Anna and Ein Shemer are recommended by the Agricultural Research Institute Tarnab, Peshawar). Dorsett Golden gives the most fruit; Anna spreads wide and has big, juicy, attractive fruit that ripens early but is slightly sour. These ripen in the last week of June or early July.
Cold hilly areas: Red Delicious, Golden Delicious, Starking Delicious, Amri, Kulu, Sky Spur and Mashadi, for taste, colour and high yield.
Rootstocks: the local small (wild) apple is the usual rootstock. East Malling rootstocks MM-106 and M-9 keep the tree smaller, and give more fruit, earlier.
aspects.sowing:
Propagation: by budding (late spring and the monsoon) or grafting (winter).
Planting an orchard: level the land in November. On wild-apple rootstock, space plants 6 m apart with rows 6 m apart; dig pits 2 x 2 x 2 (feet). On dwarf rootstocks, 5 x 5 m is enough. In mid December fill the pits with equal parts soil, silt (bhal) and well-rotted farmyard manure, and water them. In mid January plant healthy grafted plants from a nursery, keeping the graft joint 10 to 12 cm above the ground.
Intercropping: in a properly laid-out orchard, other crops can be grown between rows for the first 4 to 5 years until the trees bear fruit: legumes, chillies, potato and onion. Add extra manure and fertilizer before these crops to keep the soil fertile.
aspects.fertilizer:
Apple needs nitrogen, phosphorus and potash. Amounts per tree by age:
At planting (in the pit): 20 kg farmyard manure and 2 kg single super phosphate.
Year 2: 10 kg manure and 250 g urea. Year 3: 10 kg manure and 370 g urea.
Year 4: 15 kg manure, 500 g urea and 1 kg single super phosphate.
Year 5: 20 kg manure, 750 g urea and 1.25 kg single super phosphate.
Years 6 to 11: 30 kg manure, 1 kg urea, 2 kg single super phosphate and 1 kg sulphate of potash.
Over 11 years: 40 kg manure, 1.5 kg urea, 3 kg single super phosphate and 1.5 kg sulphate of potash.
Timing: put well-rotted manure in December and January. Give chemical fertilizer in two equal parts: one a week before flowering and one after fruit set. Water right after applying fertilizer.
aspects.irrigation: Irrigation depends on rainfall, temperature, wind and soil. In hot, dry summer weather water young plants about every 7 days and big trees every 12 to 15 days; on sandy or light soil water more often. In winter 2 to 3 irrigations are enough. Stop watering before fruit set and again before ripening: the fruit ripens on time with better colour and texture. Water big trees by flooding small basins, and young plants through furrows. Too much water causes root and collar rot.
aspects.pests_diseases:
Main problems: black aphid, codling moth, apple scab and root rot.
Black aphid: appears a few days after fruit set, stuck behind the flower and on the fruit stalk. Spray an insecticide such as Karate at 2 cc per litre of water.
Codling moth: the female lays eggs at the end of April or early May; the larva enters the fruit from the flower end and eats the pulp. Attacked fruit is small and shrivelled with a hole. Spray Supracide or Karate at 2 cc per litre of water.
Apple scab: small black spots on leaves and fruit that spread as the fruit ripens, and the fruit rots inside. Spray Dithane M-45 at 2 g per litre after winter pruning and again at the start of the monsoon.
Root and collar rot: a fungus attacks the stem and roots at ground level during long rains or over-watering, and the bark and roots rot. Reduce watering, don't let water stand around the tree, and pour Dithane M-45 at 2 g per litre of water at the roots.
Do not hoe right after spraying: dust can carry the chemical into the farmer's body.
aspects.harvesting: Pick apples by hand when the fruit's natural colour shows clearly, at intervals, without damaging the fruit or the spurs. For a better price, grade the fruit by size, wrap each in thin paper, pack in wooden crates, and keep it in cold storage before taking it to the mandi. Anna, Dorsett Golden and Gold Summer ripen in the last week of June or early July.
aspects.machinery: Training and pruning: shape young trees during the first 4 to 5 years so the trees are strong and later pruning is easier. Two systems are used: central leader and modified central leader. Pruning strengthens the trunk, lets in air and light, and stops branches breaking under fruit load or storms. Pruning is skilled work: have it done only by experienced people, or it can do more harm than good.
aspects.other: Intercrops in young orchards (first 4 to 5 years): legumes, chillies, potato and onion, with extra manure and fertilizer to keep the soil fertile.

timing.sowing: plant grafted trees in mid January (pits prepared November to mid December)
timing.harvesting: late June to early July for Anna, Dorsett Golden and Gold Summer
